def check_smaller(tup1: tuple, tup2: tuple) -> bool:
    """
    Check if each element of the second tuple is smaller than its corresponding 
    element in the first tuple. Returns True only if ALL elements satisfy this condition; otherwise False.
    
    Assumes both tuples have equal length (as implied by "corresponding").
    """
    # Optional: assert len(tup1) == len(tup2), but we'll handle it gracefully or let Python raise an error naturally
    
    for a, b in zip(tup1, tup2):
        if not (b < a):  # i.e., if b >= a
            return False
    return True


# Example test cases:
assert check_smaller((1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 4)) == False   # because 2 is NOT smaller than 1 → returns False immediately
assert check_smaller((5, 6, 7), (4, 5, 6)) == True    # all elements in second are strictly less
assert check_smaller((10,), (9,)) == True              # single element case

print("All assertions passed.")
